title: What Maker District Cities Is
definition: Maker District Cities: cities built around fabrication and workshops.
description:
Maker District Cities — Signature Edition: cities built around fabrication and workshops. This is the JAH-original vision, designed from first principles and labeled as Signature speculation throughout.

The Signature maker hulls program starts where public roadmaps stop. Where public research asks what is fundable, the Signature line asks what is buildable: workshop districts rethought, cargo transit rebuilt, tool libraries reimagined for the century ahead. Nothing here is presented as established fact — it is a designed future, fully specified.

This edition mirrors the public database record for record — concept, components, milestones, demos, drills, alliance, roadmap — but every entry is the Signature take: bolder timelines, integrated systems thinking, and the forge blocks ambition that defines the Signature line.

t: The Signature Vision: Maker District Cities
title: The Signature Vision: Maker District Cities
definition: The JAH-original Signature vision of Maker District Cities.
description:
The Signature vision of Maker District Cities does not ask what committees will fund — it asks what physics allows and what engineering can compound.

Signature maker hulls program, charter one: master workshop districts at laboratory scale within the decade. Charter two: scale cargo transit manufacturing until cost collapses. Charter three: operate tool libraries systems continuously, learning in public, improving every cycle.

This is a Signature concept — original JAH speculation, fully specified and honestly labeled. The public edition of this database carries the documented research record; this edition carries the bolder integrated vision: what Maker District Cities becomes when every piece is designed to work with every other piece from day one.

In the Maker District Cities architecture, the maker hulls grid is load-bearing: without it the maker hulls fails outright — Maker District Cities stops being Maker District Cities at all. Builders sequence this piece early because every other component assumes it works. In the Signature architecture this piece is designed first-class, not bolted on.

t: 2030 — The first maker hulls district opens at 50
title: 2030 — The first maker hulls district opens at 50
definition: 2030 milestone on the Maker District Cities roadmap.
description:
The first maker hulls district opens at 50,000 residents, its workshop districts grid and cargo transit mobility running at full design load.

What must be true first: the workshop districts results have to replicate outside the lab, cargo transit manufacturing must reach pilot scale, and tool libraries operations need a year of continuous runtime. Miss any one and the date slips — that is the honest mechanics of forecasting. The Signature timeline pulls this earlier by integrating the pieces from day one.

Signals to watch: peer-reviewed workshop districts demonstrations, cargo transit cost curves bending down, and operators — not vendors — reporting tool libraries uptime. When all three flash green, 2030 stops being a forecast and starts being a schedule. (4 years from the 2026 baseline.)
key_points: Target year: 2030 (4 years out).
Depends on: workshop districts, cargo transit, tool libraries.

title: Readiness Estimator: Maker District Cities
definition: Estimates Maker District Cities readiness from component maturity.
description:
The estimator scores the six Maker District Cities components on the TRL 1–9 scale and averages them into a verdict: research phase, pilot phase, or deployment phase. Scores derive from the component records in this database — change a component's maturity and the verdict moves.

Honest scoring is the point: a maker hulls that averages TRL 3 is not failing, it is three phases from deployment, and the estimator tells you which component drags the average down. Fund that one first.

title: Maker District Cities Systems Simulator
definition: Simulates Maker District Cities operating for a day.
description:
The simulator walks a Maker District Cities installation through six operating steps, with seeded randomness standing in for real-world variation. Seed 40703 reproduces this exact run — change the seed in the program to explore other days.

Watch for DEGRADED steps: they mark where workshop districts monitoring, cargo transit redundancy, or tool libraries maintenance would intervene in a real deployment. A simulator that never degrades is lying; this one degrades about eight percent of the time, like early hardware does.

title: Maker District Cities Master Roadmap
definition: The united roadmap for Maker District Cities: prove, build, operate, compound.
description:
The master roadmap for Maker District Cities — cities built around fabrication and workshops.

Phase 1 — Prove (workshop districts): laboratory demonstrations of every component, replicated independently. No scaling until the physics is boring.

Phase 2 — Build (cargo transit): pilot manufacturing and integration. The six pieces meet for the first time and the interfaces get honest.

Phase 3 — Operate (tool libraries): continuous real-world operation. Uptime, cost curves and failure data replace projections.

Phase 4 — Compound (forge blocks): maker hulls as everyday infrastructure. Costs collapse, standards settle, and industrial edge-scale deployment begins.

Signature edition: phases overlap aggressively — integration starts on day one. This record unites the database: overview, research, components, milestones, demos and drills all point here.

Each phase has exit criteria.
Unites all 20 records.
